summary:
MARS SURVIVE 360 is an intelligent Mars mission planning and astronaut survival platform designed to support safer and more informed exploration of the Martian surface, with a focus on Jezero Crater.
We developed an integrated web-based system that combines 2D and 3D Mars mapping, terrain analysis, route planning, hazard assessment, autonomous navigation support, and mission resource management. The platform evaluates alternative routes by considering distance, slope, terrain hazards, oxygen consumption, energy requirements, communication availability, and emergency return scenarios. It also incorporates AI-based traversability analysis and integrated mission intelligence to support decision-making.
MARS SURVIVE 360 addresses a critical challenge of human Mars exploration: how to plan missions while minimizing risks and ensuring that astronauts can safely complete their objectives and return to their base. By bringing geospatial data, scientific models, simulations, and mission planning tools into one environment, the platform helps users understand potential dangers before making operational decisions.
Our goal is to transform Mars exploration data into practical survival-oriented decisions, contributing to safer, smarter, and more sustainable future human missions to Mars.
details:
MARS SURVIVE 360: An intelligent platform for Mars mission planning and astronaut survival

MARS SURVIVE 360 is an intelligent web-based platform designed to support the planning of human exploration missions on the surface of Mars, assess potential hazards, and improve astronaut safety. The project focuses on the Jezero Crater region and combines geospatial analysis, route-planning algorithms, artificial intelligence, and mission resource simulations.

How the project works: The platform provides interactive 2D and 3D maps of Mars, terrain analysis tools, and surface traversability assessment. Users can plan routes between selected locations, compare alternative paths, and choose a route strategy based on distance, terrain slope, surface roughness, and potential hazards.

The system uses A*, Weighted A*, and Dijkstra algorithms for route planning. It supports four strategies: shortest route, lowest-slope route, lowest-hazard route, and balanced route.

The platform also estimates oxygen and energy consumption, identifies an estimated turn-back point, evaluates communication coverage, and simulates selected emergency scenarios. Its machine-learning module assesses terrain traversability using available geospatial data.

Project Benefits: The main advantage of MARS SURVIVE 360 is its integrated approach to mission planning. Instead of considering distance alone, the platform evaluates several factors that may affect the safety and efficiency of movement across the Martian surface.

Key benefits include:

  • Comparing multiple alternative routes.
  • Analyzing terrain and identifying potentially hazardous areas.
  • Estimating oxygen and energy requirements.
  • Identifying an estimated safe return point.
  • Assessing risks and simulating emergency scenarios.
  • Visualizing mission-planning results through interactive maps.
  • Bringing geospatial data, algorithms, and analytical tools together in one platform.

Expected Impact: The project aims to contribute to the development of decision-support tools for future human missions to Mars. Its expected impact is to improve preliminary route planning, support more efficient resource allocation, and help identify potential hazards before and during mission planning.

In the future, this approach could be useful to researchers, aerospace engineers, mission planners, and educational institutions. The platform can also serve as an experimental environment for studying autonomous navigation, geospatial analysis, and space exploration simulations.

Technologies and tools used. The project was developed using the following technologies:

  • Programming language: Python.
  • Web application framework: Streamlit.
  • Geospatial visualization: Folium, Streamlit-Folium, PyDeck.
  • Data visualization and analytics: Plotly, Matplotlib.
  • Data processing: NumPy, Pandas, SciPy.
  • Machine learning: Scikit-learn; PyTorch is supported as an optional tool.
  • Geospatial processing: Rasterio, Shapely, and optionally GeoPandas.
  • Route planning and graph algorithms: A*, Weighted A*, Dijkstra, NetworkX.
  • Backend and API: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic.
  • Image processing: OpenCV, Pillow.
  • Astronomical data processing: Astropy.
  • Version control and source-code hosting: Git and GitHub.

The platform is designed to work with geospatial datasets, including Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and images of the Martian surface. Open scientific data sources, including NASA and USGS datasets, are used where available. Real observations, synthetic terrain models, and simulation outputs are identified separately to avoid confusing measured data with calculated assumptions.

Creativity and Innovation: The creativity of MARS SURVIVE 360 lies in combining several aspects of space exploration into one interactive platform. The system treats route planning not simply as finding the shortest path, but as a multi-factor decision-making problem involving terrain conditions, potential hazards, energy consumption, oxygen requirements, and return feasibility.

An important innovative element is the combination of algorithmic route planning with machine-learning-based terrain traversability assessment. Users can compare different route strategies, examine their characteristics, and evaluate the possible consequences of their choices.

As a result, MARS SURVIVE 360 is more than a map of Mars: it is an experimental intelligent environment for simulating and supporting the planning of human exploration missions.

Factors Considered by the Team. During development, the team considered the following factors:

  • Terrain characteristics and geological features of Jezero Crater.
  • Surface slopes, roughness, and potentially hazardous areas.
  • Limited oxygen supplies and energy resources.
  • The importance of planning a safe return.
  • Possible communication limitations between astronauts, rovers, and orbital relay systems.
  • Potential emergency and abnormal mission scenarios.
  • Reliability, origin, and quality of scientific source data.
  • Platform performance, interface usability, and accessibility.
  • Future scalability and the possibility of integrating additional scientific datasets and algorithms.

MARS SURVIVE 360 is an experimental research prototype and decision-support tool. Its calculations and simulations do not replace certified safety systems and should not be considered operational instructions for real crewed missions.
